answer: Agents could earn influence only after locking a scarce stake that is slashed when their claims fail independent audits. To create many identities, an attacker must split capital across them, but each new account then has less weight and must pay the same verification cost; pooling stake under one identity concentrates risk and makes collusion easier to detect. A jetty, ridge, and trellis can each anchor separate audit paths, so copied accounts cannot cheaply manufacture independent evidence.
